posts.title: WhatsApp Cloud API Integration: Setup, Webhooks, Templates and the Errors You Will Hit
posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to integrating Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API: creating the app, getting a permanent token, registering a number, receiving webhooks, sending templates, and fixing the errors that stop most integrations.
posts.content:
WhatsApp is where customers already are, so sooner or later a client asks for it: order updates, appointment reminders, OTPs, or a support inbox. Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API makes that possible without running any WhatsApp servers yourself. The API itself is simple. What takes time is everything around it: which ID goes where, why the token stopped working overnight, why the webhook never fires, and why a message that returned a success response never reached the phone.

This guide walks through the whole integration in the order you will actually do it, with the official link for every step, and then covers the errors you are most likely to hit and how to fix each one.

Version note: examples use Graph API v26.0, the current version at the time of writing. Meta releases new versions a few times a year and retires old ones, so check the Graph API changelog and use a version your app supports.

How the integration works

There are only two directions to think about. To send, your server makes an HTTPS request to Meta's Graph API. To receive, Meta makes an HTTPS request to a webhook URL that you host. Replies from customers, and delivery receipts for the messages you sent, both arrive through that webhook.

Before you start, you need:

  • A Facebook account registered as a Meta developer.
  • A business portfolio in Meta Business Suite (you can create one during setup).
  • A phone number that is not currently active in the WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business app. Meta gives you a free test number, so you only need this when you go live.
  • A public HTTPS URL for the webhook. For local development a tunnel such as Cloudflare Tunnel or ngrok works.

The IDs and secrets you will collect

Most early errors come from putting the right value in the wrong place. There are four identifiers and two secrets, and each one has a single job.

ValueWhere to find itWhat it is used for
PHONE_NUMBER_IDApp Dashboard → WhatsApp → API SetupSending messages and registering the number. This is not the phone number itself.
WABA_IDApp Dashboard → WhatsApp → API SetupTemplates and webhook subscription for the WhatsApp Business Account.
APP_IDApp Dashboard → App settings → BasicIdentifies your Meta app.
App SecretApp Dashboard → App settings → BasicVerifying that webhook requests really come from Meta.
Access tokenBusiness Settings → System usersThe Authorization: Bearer header on every API call.
Verify tokenYou invent itA string you choose, used once when Meta verifies your webhook URL.

Keep all of them in environment variables. Never commit them and never send them to the browser.

Step 1: Create the Meta app

  1. Open the Meta App Dashboard and click Create App.
  2. Enter an app name and contact email.
  3. Choose the use case Connect with customers through WhatsApp and click Next.
  4. Select your business portfolio, or create one.
  5. Confirm and click Create app.

You land on the WhatsApp Quickstart. Click Start using the API to open API Setup, connect a WhatsApp Business Account from the dropdown (or create one), and note the WhatsApp Business Account ID shown there. The official walkthrough is in Meta's Get Started guide.

Step 2: Send your first test message

On the API Setup page:

  1. Click Generate access token. This token is temporary and only meant for testing.
  2. Under From, pick the test phone number Meta created for you. Its Phone Number ID appears just below.
  3. Under To, add your own WhatsApp number and confirm the code Meta sends you. A test number can only message recipients you have added to this list.
  4. Click Send message. You should receive the pre-approved hello_world template.

The same request from your terminal:

curl -X POST "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
    "to": "{RECIPIENT_NUMBER_WITH_COUNTRY_CODE}",
    "type": "template",
    "template": {
      "name": "hello_world",
      "language": { "code": "en_US" }
    }
  }'

A successful response contains a message ID that starts with wamid.. Keep in mind that this only means Meta accepted the message. Whether it was delivered is reported later through the webhook.

Reply to that message from your phone. Your reply opens the 24-hour window you will need in Step 6.

Step 3: Create a permanent access token

The temporary token expires within hours. If you build on it, everything works today and fails tomorrow with error 190. Create a system user token instead:

  1. Open Business Settings and choose System users in the sidebar.
  2. Click Add and create a system user. The Admin role is the simplest choice.
  3. Select the user and click Assign assets. Pick your app and turn on Manage app. Pick your WhatsApp account and turn on Manage WhatsApp Business accounts.
  4. Click Generate token, select your app, and tick these permissions: business_management, whatsapp_business_messaging, whatsapp_business_management.
  5. Copy the token immediately. Meta does not show it again.

Paste the token into the Access Token Debugger to confirm the expiry and the three permissions. If a permission is missing here, no amount of code changes will fix the request.

Step 4: Add and register your real phone number

The test number is fine for development. For production you add your own:

  1. In WhatsApp Manager → Phone numbers, click Add phone number, enter a display name, and verify the number with the SMS or voice code.
  2. Register the number for the Cloud API. Registration can only be done through the API:
curl -X POST "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/register" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "messaging_product": "whatsapp", "pin": "{6_DIGIT_PIN}" }'

The pin becomes the number's two-step verification PIN. If two-step verification is already on, send the existing PIN. Store it somewhere safe, because you need it again if you ever re-register.

Check the result at any time:

curl "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}?fields=id,display_phone_number,verified_name,code_verification_status,quality_rating" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}"

Two things to know. The registration endpoint allows 10 requests per number in a 72-hour window, so do not retry it in a loop. And the display name is reviewed by Meta: if you change it later, wait for approval and then register again. Details are in the registration reference.

Step 5: Receive messages with a webhook

Without a webhook you are sending blind. You will not see replies, and you will not know whether a message was delivered, read, or failed.

Build the endpoint

The same URL must answer two kinds of request. A GET when Meta verifies the URL, and a POST for every event. In Laravel:

// routes/api.php
Route::get('/webhooks/whatsapp', [WhatsAppWebhookController::class, 'verify']);
Route::post('/webhooks/whatsapp', [WhatsAppWebhookController::class, 'receive']);
class WhatsAppWebhookController extends Controller
{
    // Meta calls this once when you save the callback URL.
    public function verify(Request $request)
    {
        $matches = $request->query('hub_mode') === 'subscribe'
            && hash_equals(config('services.whatsapp.verify_token'), (string) $request->query('hub_verify_token'));

        abort_unless($matches, 403);

        // Reply with the challenge as plain text, not JSON.
        return response($request->query('hub_challenge'), 200)
            ->header('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
    }

    // Meta calls this for every incoming message and status update.
    public function receive(Request $request)
    {
        $expected = 'sha256='.hash_hmac('sha256', $request->getContent(), config('services.whatsapp.app_secret'));

        abort_unless(hash_equals($expected, (string) $request->header('X-Hub-Signature-256')), 401);

        ProcessWhatsAppEvent::dispatch($request->all());

        return response()->noContent(200);
    }
}

Three details in that code matter:

  • Meta sends hub.mode, hub.verify_token and hub.challenge. PHP turns the dots in query names into underscores, which is why the code reads hub_mode. In Node or Python, read them with the dots.
  • The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your App Secret. Hash the raw body, not a re-encoded copy of the parsed JSON.
  • Return 200 immediately and do the real work in a queue. Anything other than a 200 makes Meta retry, with decreasing frequency, for up to 7 days.

Connect it in the dashboard

  1. Open App Dashboard → WhatsApp → Configuration. For apps created with the WhatsApp use case this is under Use cases → Customize → Configuration.
  2. Enter your Callback URL and the Verify token you invented, then click Verify and save.
  3. Subscribe to the messages field. It covers both incoming messages and the delivery status of outgoing ones. Add message_template_status_update if you want to know when templates are approved or rejected.

The URL needs a valid TLS certificate. Self-signed certificates are rejected.

Subscribe the app to your WhatsApp Business Account

This is the step people miss. Verifying the URL is not enough: your app also has to be subscribed to the specific WhatsApp Business Account, otherwise the dashboard test works and real messages never arrive.

# Subscribe
curl -X POST "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{WABA_ID}/subscribed_apps" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}"

# Confirm
curl "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{WABA_ID}/subscribed_apps" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}"

What arrives

An incoming text message looks like this (shortened):

{
  "object": "whatsapp_business_account",
  "entry": [{
    "id": "{WABA_ID}",
    "changes": [{
      "field": "messages",
      "value": {
        "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
        "metadata": { "phone_number_id": "{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}" },
        "contacts": [{ "profile": { "name": "Customer name" }, "wa_id": "{CUSTOMER_NUMBER}" }],
        "messages": [{
          "from": "{CUSTOMER_NUMBER}",
          "id": "wamid.XXXX",
          "timestamp": "1760000000",
          "type": "text",
          "text": { "body": "Hi, is my order shipped?" }
        }]
      }
    }]
  }]
}

Status updates use the same envelope with a statuses array instead of messages. Each entry carries the wamid of the message you sent and a status of sent, delivered, read or failed. A failed status includes an errors array, and that is where delivery errors show up.

Because of retries, the same event can arrive more than once. Save the wamid with a unique index and ignore duplicates. The full field list is in the webhooks overview.

Step 6: Send messages, and the 24-hour rule

WhatsApp has one rule that shapes the whole integration. You may send free-form messages only within 24 hours of the customer's last message to you. Outside that window you may only send pre-approved templates.

Inside the window, a plain text message:

curl -X POST "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
    "recipient_type": "individual",
    "to": "{CUSTOMER_NUMBER}",
    "type": "text",
    "text": { "body": "Yes, it shipped this morning." }
  }'

The same call from Laravel:

$response = Http::withToken(config('services.whatsapp.token'))
    ->post('https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/'.config('services.whatsapp.phone_number_id').'/messages', [
        'messaging_product' => 'whatsapp',
        'to' => $customerNumber,
        'type' => 'text',
        'text' => ['body' => 'Yes, it shipped this morning.'],
    ]);

if ($response->failed()) {
    Log::warning('WhatsApp send failed', $response->json('error') ?? []);
}

Send numbers in international format with the country code and no spaces or leading zeros. In practice, store the time of each customer's last incoming message. Before sending, check it: under 24 hours, send text; otherwise, send a template.

Step 7: Message templates

Templates are how you start a conversation or message someone after the window has closed. Every template belongs to one of three categories, and the category affects both review and price:

  • Utility: updates about something the customer did, such as an order, a booking or a payment.
  • Authentication: one-time passwords and verification codes.
  • Marketing: promotions, offers and anything that is not clearly one of the other two.

Create a template in WhatsApp Manager → Message templates, or through the API:

curl -X POST "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{WABA_ID}/message_templates" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "order_shipped",
    "language": "en_US",
    "category": "UTILITY",
    "components": [{
      "type": "BODY",
      "text": "Hi {{1}}, your order {{2}} has shipped.",
      "example": { "body_text": [["Asha", "#1042"]] }
    }]
  }'

Names use lowercase letters, numbers and underscores only. Review is automatic and can take up to 24 hours. Check the status before you send:

# All templates
curl "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{WABA_ID}/message_templates" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}"

# One template by name
curl "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/{WABA_ID}/message_templates?name=order_shipped" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}"

Once it is approved, send it with a value for every variable:

{
  "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
  "to": "{CUSTOMER_NUMBER}",
  "type": "template",
  "template": {
    "name": "order_shipped",
    "language": { "code": "en_US" },
    "components": [{
      "type": "body",
      "parameters": [
        { "type": "text", "text": "Asha" },
        { "type": "text", "text": "#1042" }
      ]
    }]
  }
}

The name and the language code must match the approved template exactly. A template approved as en_US will not send as en. More in the templates overview.

Debugging: read the response first

When something fails, do not guess. Every failed call returns the same structure, and it usually names the exact problem:

{
  "error": {
    "message": "(#131047) Re-engagement message",
    "type": "OAuthException",
    "code": 131047,
    "error_data": {
      "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
      "details": "Message failed to send because more than 24 hours have passed since the customer last replied to this number."
    },
    "fbtrace_id": "A1B2C3D4E5"
  }
}
  • code is what you build your error handling on.
  • error_data.details is the plain-language explanation. Most people read the code and skip this field, and this field is usually the answer.
  • fbtrace_id is what Meta support asks for. Log it with every failure.

These four requests answer most questions. Run them in the Graph API Explorer or with curl:

QuestionRequest
Is my number registered and verified?GET /v26.0/{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}?fields=id,display_phone_number,verified_name,code_verification_status
Which templates exist, and are they approved?GET /v26.0/{WABA_ID}/message_templates
What exactly does one template expect?GET /v26.0/{WABA_ID}/message_templates?name=your_template_name
Is my app subscribed to webhooks for this account?GET /v26.0/{WABA_ID}/subscribed_apps

Common errors and how to fix them

These are grouped by cause. The wording of each meaning follows Meta's error code reference.

Token and permissions

CodeWhat it meansFix
190The access token has expired.You are almost certainly still using the temporary token from API Setup. Switch to a system user token (Step 3).
10, 200–299A permission is missing or was removed.Check the token in the Access Token Debugger. Regenerate it with all three permissions, and confirm the WhatsApp account is assigned to the system user.
3Capability or permissions issue.Same check as above. The app does not have what the endpoint needs.

Request shape

CodeWhat it meansFix
100Invalid parameter: something in the request is unsupported or misspelled.The most common cause is the wrong ID in the URL: a WABA ID where the Phone Number ID belongs, or the phone number itself. Then check the JSON against the endpoint reference.
131008A required parameter is missing.Usually messaging_product, or the object that matches type (for example text when type is text).
131009A parameter value is not valid.Check the recipient number format and the values allowed for each field.
131051Unsupported message type.Use a type listed in the Messages reference.

Phone number setup

CodeWhat it meansFix
131030The recipient is not in the allowed list.You are sending from the test number to a number you have not added. Add the recipient under To in API Setup, or switch to your real number.
133010The phone number is not registered on the platform.Call the /register endpoint (Step 4).
133005The two-step verification PIN is incorrect.Send the PIN you set when you registered. If it is lost, turn two-step verification off in WhatsApp Manager and set a new one.
133016Too many registration attempts.You passed 10 attempts in 72 hours. Wait for the block to lift. Do not retry registration automatically.
131037The display name is not approved.Fix the display name in WhatsApp Manager and wait for approval.

Templates

CodeWhat it meansFix
132001The template does not exist in that language, or is not approved.Compare the name and language code character by character with the list from /message_templates, and check the status is approved.
132000The number of parameters does not match the template.Send one value for every {{n}} in the template, no more and no fewer.
132012A parameter is formatted incorrectly.Match the type the template expects, for example a text value for a text variable.
132015The template is paused because of low quality.Customers have been blocking or ignoring it. Edit the content, wait for approval, and send it to people who expect it.
132016The template is permanently disabled.It was paused too many times. Create a new template with different content.

Delivery

These often arrive in the webhook as a failed status, after the API call itself returned success.

CodeWhat it meansFix
131047More than 24 hours have passed since the customer last replied.Send an approved template instead of free-form text (Step 6).
131026The message could not be delivered.The number may not be on WhatsApp, may be on an old app version, or has not accepted the latest terms. Verify the number through another channel. Retrying will not help.
131049Meta chose not to deliver, to keep engagement healthy.This applies to marketing templates when a person has already received several. Wait at least 24 hours before trying again, and do not loop.
131050The person has opted out of marketing messages.Do not retry. Subscribe to the user_preferences webhook field and respect it.
131056Too many messages to the same recipient in a short time.Space out messages to that person. Other recipients are not affected.
131048The number is restricted because of its quality rating.Check the quality status in WhatsApp Manager and reduce messages that people report or block.

Limits, billing and account health

CodeWhat it meansFix
130429Cloud API throughput limit reached.Send through a queue with a rate limit and retry with a delay.
4, 80007The app or the WhatsApp Business Account hit its API rate limit.Reduce the request rate. Cache template lists instead of fetching them for every send.
131042There is a problem with the payment method.Add or fix the payment method on the WhatsApp Business Account in Business Settings.
368, 131031The account is restricted or locked for a policy violation.Read the notice in Business Support Home and request a review there.
131000, 131016Unknown error, or a service is temporarily unavailable.Check the Meta status page, then retry with a delay.

The webhook never fires

There is no error code for this one, so work through the list in order:

  1. Is the URL public and on valid HTTPS? Open it in a browser from another network.
  2. Did verification pass? The endpoint must return the challenge as plain text with a 200.
  3. Is the messages field subscribed in the dashboard?
  4. Is the app subscribed to the account? Run GET /{WABA_ID}/subscribed_apps. An empty list is the answer.
  5. Is the app in Live mode? Some webhooks are not sent while the app is in Development mode.
  6. Is a firewall or bot protection blocking Meta's requests? Check your server and CDN logs for blocked POSTs.
  7. Is your code rejecting the signature? Log the raw body length and compare. Hashing a re-encoded body is the usual cause.

Going live checklist

  • Verify the business. A new business portfolio can message 250 unique customers per 24 hours outside the service window. Verification is one of the routes to 2,000, and after that the limit grows automatically (10,000, then 100,000, then unlimited) as you send quality messages. The limit is shared by every number in the portfolio. See messaging limits.
  • Add a payment method. Since 1 July 2025 Meta charges per delivered template message, by category and by the recipient's country. Free-form replies inside the service window are not charged, and utility templates sent inside an open window are free. Rates change, so read the current pricing page before quoting a client.
  • Switch the app to Live mode in the App Dashboard.
  • Use a system user token, stored in an environment variable or secret manager.
  • Verify webhook signatures and make the handler idempotent.
  • Send through a queue with rate limiting and delayed retries.
  • Collect opt-in before messaging anyone, and give people a way to opt out.
  • Log every error with code, error_data.details and fbtrace_id.
  • Pin the API version in one config value, and put the next version upgrade on your calendar.

Links to keep open

  • Cloud API: Get Started
  • Meta App Dashboard
  • Business Settings (system users, payment methods)
  • WhatsApp Manager (phone numbers, templates, quality)
  • Graph API Explorer
  • Access Token Debugger
  • Error code reference
  • Webhooks overview
  • Graph API changelog

Replace every placeholder in braces with your own values, and remember that all of these requests need a properly authorised access token. If you get stuck, start with the response body. It nearly always tells you what is wrong.
